name: Grey Purple
lede: Grey Purple is a muted, dusty violet, a plain descriptive name that several color systems recorded long before screens did.

notes.cite: Pastoureau, Green: The History of a Color, ch. 46 ("Green today")
ColorHub library (data/library.json): ISCC-NBS 1955 blocks 223 and 228, Ridgway 1912 pl. XXXVI, Maerz & Paul 1930 pl. 44 G 7 (1912), xkcd; CIEDE2000

sections.title: A plain description
sections.body: The books read have no entry for the pair as a color name; where they print the words together they are only items in a list [1]. Pastoureau notes that in favorite-color surveys grey and purple are "second-rank" colors that share the crumbs after blue, green and red [1]. The color itself is better documented by charts than by prose.

sections.title: On the old charts
sections.body: The library finds the color in four systems: the xkcd survey, the 1955 ISCC-NBS blocks 223 and 228, Ridgway's 1912 atlas (plate XXXVI), and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, which first records it in 1912 on plate 44 G 7 [2]. Two near-duplicate names sit within two units: Greyish Purple and Hyssop Violet [2]. Its nearest everyday name is [[mauve]], about ten and a half units away [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch is uncommon in museum paintings: 25 of 23,781 contain it, about 0.11 per cent [3]. The earliest dated painting is from 1658, by Giovanni Francesco Romanelli, and the rest of the 11 dated paintings run to 1924, so the early centuries are thin [3]. In printed English the phrase's word peaks in the 1840s, though that count covers every sense of the word [3].
